title: Every Maria Theresa thaler minted since 1780 has been dated 1780

cover.alt: A large silver coin held in the palm of a hand, showing the veiled profile of Empress Maria Theresa and a Latin legend.

body: The **Maria Theresa thaler** is a big silver coin first minted in Habsburg Austria in 1741. Empress Maria Theresa died in 1780, and every new thaler struck since then has carried that same date. The coin's reliable silver made it a favourite far from Austria: the traveller James Bruce found in 1768 that, unlike debased local money, it dominated the lands he visited, and in the Red Sea region merchants would accept no other currency. It served as money across large parts of Africa and the Middle East until after the Second World War. Between 1751 and 2000 some 389 million were minted, and the Austrian Mint still makes them.

slides.alt: An old sepia postcard of a line of laden donkeys and men in white robes outside a long low building in Dire Dawa.
slides.caption: Crates of thalers being loaded onto donkeys at Dire Dawa, Ethiopia, for the trip to Harar, on a postcard from about 1908 to 1910.

slides.question: Out of 10 parts of a Maria Theresa thaler, how many are silver?
slides.explanation: About 8: the coin is 83.3% silver and the rest copper, with 23.386 g of fine silver in a coin weighing 28.07 g.

slides.heading: Both sides minted it
slides.text: Italy held the rights to mint the coin when the Second World War began. Yet the British struck some 18 million thalers of their own at the Bombay mint, to pay for the East African Campaign that drove Italian forces out of Ethiopia.

slides.heading: True or false?

items.text: Each coin shows the year it was struck
It holds over 23 g of fine silver
It was only ever used in Europe

slides.explanation: Every new thaler says 1780, whenever it was made, and it was used from Ethiopia and Somalia to Yemen and Oman.

slides.question: Around the rim of the coin runs the motto of Maria Theresa's reign. What is it?
slides.explanation: Justitia et Clementia: justice and mercy.
